summary: VectorCraft is a drawing app, like Adobe Illustrator. It stores each drawing as lines and shapes (vector graphics). The drawing stays sharp at every size. Use it for logos, icons, charts and illustrations.
use_cases: Make a chart for a report from a small table of numbers, in your own colours.
Design a logo or a badge for a club, an event or a small business.
Export 1 design as PNG for social media, SVG for a website and PDF for print.
Save the list of steps once. Then make a new chart every month with new numbers.
story: VectorCraft drew the badge and 3 charts for the poster and the slides. Its chart tool drew the share of the conversation per month. It also drew the share of negative posts per theme and the sample by platform. The key themes have strong colours, and the other themes are grey. VectorCraft built the badge from simple shapes, text on a curve, a shadow and a glow. DesignCraft and DeckCraft used these files.
recipe: vectorcraft-cli run --cmd graph.create --params "$(cat graph.json)" --export chart.svg --export chart.png
vectorcraft-cli run --in chart.svg --cmd select.all --cmd type.createOutlines --export chart.pdf
recipe_note: Draw a chart from the numbers in graph.json. Change its text to shapes for print. Export the badge at 2 times its size.

headless_notes: All files come from vectorcraft-cli run without a window. The mcp command was not used. graph.create drew every chart from the numbers in summary.json. Series colours go on the series group, and the graph keeps them. On a line chart, a fill on the series group also fills the line, so the script removes that fill. The chart tool has no data labels, so text.create added the end values at calculated positions. A probe run read the object ids for the label style; the ids stay the same for the same steps. The poster and deck charts use the same steps. They hide the title and use a smaller artboard.
